flags: WYDOT brochure is dated May 1, 2000. Seasonal closure is corroborated by the tourism cache; the checked date records this cache review, not live road status. Exact reopening dates and old interpretive-tour arrangements omitted.

No Tribal-authored page is cached. Nation names and the attributed Crow statement follow cache/04.txt; no construction date or builder is asserted. Cache/04.txt attributes the solstice alignment to astronomer John Eddy. The current unqualified claim is omitted rather than presented as an established original purpose; disputed stellar alignments in cache/06.txt are a separate issue.
The cache disagrees on wheel diameter (75 feet, 80 feet and around 80 feet); measurement omitted.
The state tourism text misleadingly says the 27-mile byway runs nearly the length of US 14A; cache/03.txt gives approximately 99 miles for the full highway. The story distinguishes their extents.
Bald Mountain City and North Tongue River moments are shorter than 90 words because the cached descriptions are thin. Road history supports renumbering, not a construction or campaigning narrative.
Medicine Wheel approach distance comes from the 2000 WYDOT brochure; no current site-manager trail or ceremony-access guidance is cached.
Formal National Forest designation tier is not established in the cached text.
